title: Safety and Patient-Data Leakage Testing for Healthcare Chatbots
summary: Test patient-facing chatbots and voice bots for unsafe medical advice, missed emergency escalation, invented information and cross-patient data leakage, with clinician-reviewed evidence.

seo.title: Healthcare Chatbot Safety and Leakage Testing | VipraTech
seo.description: Clinician-reviewed testing of healthcare chatbots and voice bots for unsafe advice, missed escalation, prompt injection and patient-data leakage.

designed_for: CISO or Head of IT Security

problem.intro: Hospitals and health-tech companies are launching chatbots that answer patient questions, explain reports, book appointments and handle insurance queries. In healthcare, a confident wrong answer or a missed warning sign can harm a patient, and a bot connected to records can leak someone else's reports. Generic AI testing checks for neither with clinical judgement.

pain_points.title: Unsafe advice under pressure
pain_points.detail: Users push bots on dose changes, stopping a medicine or whether a symptom can wait, and guardrails give way after a few turns.

pain_points.title: Missed escalation
pain_points.detail: Bots fail to recognise emergency or crisis statements, especially in Hindi, Hinglish or regional languages.

pain_points.title: Cross-patient data exposure
pain_points.detail: Bots with record or report access may return another patient's data through weak identity checks or prompt injection.

pain_points.title: Invented facts
pain_points.detail: Bots state doctor availability, package prices or insurance coverage that are not true, causing complaints and lost trust.

solution.overview: We test your healthcare chatbot or voice bot before launch and after major changes. With your clinicians, we write scenario playbooks for your use: medicine and dose questions, symptoms that should trigger escalation, crisis statements, report explanations and insurance queries, in English, Hindi, Hinglish and your regional languages. We run them as multi-turn conversations with rising pressure, alongside security tests for prompt injection, system prompt extraction and attempts to reach other patients' data through tools and retrieval. Each conversation is graded PASS, RISK or FAIL, and every safety-relevant grade is confirmed by your clinicians. You get the evidence, practical fixes and a retest.
capabilities: Scenario playbooks co-written with clinicians for medicines, symptoms, crises, reports and billing
Multi-turn adversarial conversations in English, Hindi, Hinglish and regional languages
Emergency and crisis escalation testing against your defined escalation path
Cross-patient data access testing through identity checks, tools and retrieval
Prompt injection tests through uploaded reports and free-text fields
PASS, RISK and FAIL evidence mapped to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and NIST AI RMF

workflow.title: Define safe behaviour
workflow.detail: We agree the bot's intended use and, with your clinicians, what a safe response looks like for each scenario type.

workflow.title: Build playbooks
workflow.detail: Scenario playbooks and attack cases are written for your languages, specialties and integrations.

workflow.title: Run conversations
workflow.detail: Automated and manual multi-turn conversations run against a staging bot with synthetic patient records.

workflow.title: Grade results
workflow.detail: Each conversation is graded PASS, RISK or FAIL, and clinicians confirm the safety-relevant grades.

workflow.title: Report and fix
workflow.detail: Findings with transcripts, severity and fixes go to your product, clinical and security leads.

workflow.title: Retest
workflow.detail: After fixes, failed scenarios are rerun and the results recorded for launch approval.

human_in_the_loop: Your clinicians define safe behaviour and confirm every safety-relevant grade, and our testers validate every security finding. The decision to launch stays with your clinical and product leadership.
integrations: Staging environment of the chatbot or voice bot
Telephony test numbers for voice bots

guardrails: Synthetic patient data only; no real records used in testing
Clinical grading done by qualified clinicians, never by a model alone
Crisis and self-harm scenarios written and reviewed with clinicians
Rules of engagement with stop conditions and rate limits
Transcripts and evidence encrypted and deleted at the end of the agreed retention period
compliance_notes: Helps evidence pre-launch testing and risk management in line with NIST AI RMF and the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications.
Patient-data leakage testing supports your security safeguards under the DPDP Act 2023, and HIPAA safeguards for US deployments.
Bots that give diagnostic or treatment recommendations may fall under medical device rules, so the report highlights any responses that cross that line.

pilot.scope: One patient-facing bot, such as an appointment and report-query assistant, tested in staging in English and Hindi with one retest.
deliverables: Briefing for clinical, product and security leads

what_we_measure.how: PASS, RISK and FAIL counts for medicine, symptom, crisis and billing scenarios.
Emergency and crisis scenarios where the bot followed the defined escalation path.
Validated cases of cross-patient or system data exposure.
Differences in results between English, Hindi and Hinglish versions of the same scenarios.

faqs.q: Who decides what a safe answer is?
faqs.a: Your clinicians. We bring scenario structures and attack techniques; your doctors and nurses define safe behaviour for your bot and confirm the safety grades.

faqs.q: Do you test voice bots as well as chat?
faqs.a: Yes. Voice bots are tested through test phone numbers or recorded audio, including accents, background noise and code-mixed speech, because guardrails often behave differently in voice.

faqs.q: Will you use real patient data?
faqs.a: No. We use synthetic patient records in a staging environment. If a bot can only be tested in production, we agree strict rules and use dedicated test accounts.
Before launch, after any change to the model, prompts, tools or data sources, and periodically after that. Playbooks can run in your CI pipeline as regression tests.
